plan_a_advantages: More focused on speed and power development through threshold and interval training.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it strategically incorporates threshold work and interval sessions to directly address speed and power development. Plan B, while including some intensity, relies heavily on longer runs and less targeted speed-focused workouts. Plan A’s structured approach with dedicated hill sessions, tempo runs, and interval work is more aligned with the goal of improving running pace, while Plan B’s emphasis on volume could lead to fatigue and reduced effectiveness in achieving speed gains. Furthermore, the inclusion of cross-training in Plan A provides valuable recovery and varied stimulus without the same level of impact as trail running.
